docs.titre: Future with going to and will
docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Talk about the future using "going to" and "will".
- Understand the difference between plans, predictions and decisions.
- Form affirmative, negative and question sentences in the future.
- Choose the right future form for the right situation.

🔍 Warm-up
Compare: "I am going to visit my aunt on Sunday." and "I think it will rain tomorrow." Both talk about the future, but they are not used the same way. This lesson shows you when to use each one.

I. Be going to: plans and intentions
📘 Rule (functions)
We use "be going to" for:
1. Plans and intentions decided before speaking: I am going to study medicine.
2. Predictions based on what we can see now: Look at those clouds! It is going to rain.

📏 Form
subject + am / is / are + going to + base verb
- I am going to travel this summer.
- She is going to buy a new phone.
- They are going to play football later.

📏 Negative and questions
- Negative: I am not going to watch that film. He isn't going to come.
- Questions: Are you going to help me? — Yes, I am. What are you going to do?

✏️ Worked examples
- We are going to visit Carthage next week.
- Look, the glass is going to fall!
- Is she going to join the club? — No, she isn't.

II. Will: predictions, decisions, promises
📘 Rule (functions)
We use "will" for:
1. Predictions and opinions about the future: I think our team will win.
2. Quick decisions made at the moment of speaking: The phone is ringing. I will answer it.
3. Promises and offers: I will help you. I promise I will be careful.
4. Future facts: I will be thirteen next year.

📏 Form
subject + will (+ not) + base verb
- I will call you tonight.
- They will not (won't) be late.
- Will you come with us? — Yes, I will. / No, I won't.

👀 Note
"will" is the same for every subject: I will, you will, he will, we will, they will. The short form is 'll (I'll, she'll) and the negative is won't.

✏️ Worked examples
- Maybe it will be sunny tomorrow.
- Don't worry, I will help you.
- I think robots will do many jobs in the future.

III. Going to or will?
📘 Rule (comparison)
This is the key point.
- Use "going to" for plans already decided and predictions you can SEE evidence for.
- Use "will" for predictions/opinions, decisions made NOW, promises and offers.

📏 Compare
- A: We need milk. B: I will buy some. (decision now → will)
- I am going to buy milk; it's on my shopping list. (plan → going to)
- Look at the sky, it is going to snow. (evidence → going to)
- I think it will snow next winter. (opinion → will)

🛠️ Method: choosing the future form
Step 1 — Is the plan already decided, or is there visible evidence? → going to.
Step 2 — Is it an opinion, a promise, an offer or a decision made right now? → will.

IV. Future time expressions
📘 Rule (vocabulary)
Common future time markers:
- tomorrow, tonight, next week, next year, soon, later, in the future, in two days, this evening.

✏️ Worked paragraph
Next summer I am going to visit my grandparents in Tozeur. We are going to travel by train. I think it will be very hot, so I am going to take light clothes. My cousin says he will show me the desert. I am sure we will have a wonderful time.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Forgetting "to" in "going to": I am going visit → I am going to visit.
2. Adding -s or -ing after "will": She will comes / She will coming → She will come.
3. Using present simple for plans: Tomorrow I visit → Tomorrow I am going to visit / I will visit.
4. Double future: I will going to → choose one form.

⭐ Recap
- "be going to" = plans decided before, and predictions with visible evidence.
- "will" = opinions/predictions, quick decisions, promises, offers, future facts.
- Both are followed by the BASE verb.
- "will" is the same for all subjects; short forms 'll and won't.
- Choose the form according to the situation.

📘 Language bank
Time markers: tomorrow, tonight, next week, next month, next year, soon, later, in the future.
Plan verbs: visit, travel, buy, study, meet, start, join.
Useful sentences: I am going to visit my aunt on Sunday. / Look! It is going to rain. / I think our team will win. / Don't worry, I will help you. / What are you going to do this weekend?

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Choose "going to" or "will".
1. Look at those dark clouds! It (is going to / will) rain.
2. The phone is ringing. I (am going to / will) answer it.
3. I have decided: I (am going to / will) study English this summer.
4. I think our team (is going to / will) win the cup.
5. Don't worry, I (am going to / will) help you with your bags.

Exercise 2 — Complete with the correct form.
1. Tomorrow we ______ (visit) our cousins. (a plan)
2. I promise I ______ (be) careful.
3. Watch out! You ______ (drop) the glass!
4. Maybe it ______ (be) sunny at the weekend.

Exercise 3 — Write two sentences about your next holiday: one plan with "going to" and one prediction with "will".

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. is going to 2. will 3. am going to 4. will 5. will.
Exercise 2: 1. are going to visit 2. will be 3. are going to drop 4. will be.

🗣️ Speaking task
Talk to a partner about your plans for next weekend. Use "I am going to..." for your plans and "I think... will..." for your predictions about the weather or a match.

👀 Extra note
A quick reminder of the difference:
- "be going to" = a plan already decided, or a prediction you can SEE coming (dark clouds → rain).
- "will" = an opinion, a promise, an offer, or a decision made at the moment of speaking.
Both are always followed by the base verb: going to GO, will GO (never "will goes" or "will going").

🌍 Real-life English
We talk about the future all the time. When you make plans with friends, you use "going to": "We are going to watch a match on Sunday." When you offer help or make a promise, you use "will": "Don't worry, I will carry that for you." Weather forecasters mix both: "It is going to be cloudy in the morning, and I think it will rain later." Try describing your plans for tomorrow with "going to" and your hopes for next year with "will". The more you connect each form to a real situation, the easier the choice becomes.

📋 Summary
- "be going to" (am/is/are + going to + base verb) is used for plans decided before speaking and for predictions based on visible evidence (Look! It's going to rain).
- "will" (will/won't + base verb) is used for opinions and predictions, quick decisions made now, promises and offers, and future facts.
- "will" never changes with the subject (I will, she will, they will); short forms 'll and won't.
- Both forms are always followed by the BASE verb — never "will goes" or "going to visit" without "to".
- Common future time markers: tomorrow, tonight, next week, next year, soon, later, in the future.
- Quick test: decided plan or visible evidence → going to; opinion, promise or on-the-spot decision → will.

enonce.question:
Read what Asma says.
I have decided what to do this summer. In July, I am going to visit my aunt in Djerba. My brother is going to join a swimming club. We bought the bus tickets yesterday!
Look at the sky! There are big black clouds. It is going to rain.

1) Find the three verbs with “going to” in the text.
2) Which two sentences are plans decided before? Which sentence is a prediction from something we can see?
3) Complete the rule: be going to + ______ verb.
4) Write one sentence about your plan for next weekend.

Read the four short situations.
a) The phone is ringing. — I will answer it!
b) I think Tunisia will win the match tomorrow.
c) Don't worry, Mum. I will tidy my room, I promise.
d) Your bag is heavy. I will carry it for you.

1) Match each sentence (a–d) with its use: a prediction or opinion / a quick decision / a promise / an offer.
2) Complete the rule: will + ______ verb, the same for all subjects.
3) Write the short forms of: I will / will not.
4) Write one prediction about your future with I think ... will ...

Riadh's birthday party is on Saturday, but there are some problems: his friend Maha is ill and the weather is bad.

Make the sentences negative.
1) She will come.
2) They will play in the garden.
3) I will be late.
4) Write the short form of will not, then rewrite sentence 1 with it.

Read Khalil's message to his friend. There are three mistakes after will.
Hi Ahmed! I am busy now, but I will to call you tonight. My brother wills bring your book tomorrow. Don't worry, we will helping you with the Maths homework.

1) Find the three mistakes.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: after will, we use the ______ verb, without to, without -s and without -ing.

The Zouari family have decided to go to Paris in August. A neighbour asks about their plans.
| Plan | Decision |
|---|---|
| travel | by plane |
| stay | in a hotel |
| visit | the Eiffel Tower |

1) Write the neighbour's question about their plan: (they / travel) by plane?
2) Answer it with a short answer.
3) Write two more questions: (they / stay) in a hotel? — (Mrs Zouari / visit) the Eiffel Tower?
4) Why do we use “going to” here, and not “will”?
Complete (offer): The bag is heavy. I ___ help you.
Complete: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain. (evidence)
Write a sentence about your plan for the weekend.
